title: An invertible section vanishing on a nonempty open vanishes
statement: Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $W\subseteq U$ open subsets of $X$ with $W$ nonempty. If $s\in L(U)$ restricts to zero on $W$, then $s=0$.

source.place: Tag 01X5 (lemma-meromorphic-functions-integral-scheme), part (2), proof omitted; local-trivialization proof already formalized in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.IntegralSections.eq_zero_of_presheaf_map_eq_zero.

proof.text: Trivialize $L$ on open neighbourhoods $V$ of points of $U$ using [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $s|_V=a e$ with $e$ a free generator. Since $X$ is integral, any two nonempty opens meet, so $V\cap W$ is nonempty. The restricted generator cancels, and $s|_W=0$ implies $a|_{V\cap W}=0$. Injectivity of restriction for the structure sheaf, from [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] (take a germ at a point in the intersection), implies $a=0$. Thus $s$ vanishes on this cover of $U$, hence vanishes by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sections-determined-by-germs]. This is the existing proved source-library theorem; no new Lean statement is introduced.
